newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen foreign investment permits $2.1 bln since 92.
newsitem.headline: Yemen foreign investment permits $2.1 bln since 92.

text.p: Yemen said on Wednesday it had issued licences for projects with an investment value of 265.7 billion rials ($2.1 billion) since 1992.
Yemen Investment Authority (YIA) announced the figure, but did not say what proportion of the 265.7 billion rials had been invested.
The YIA statement said that up to April it had granted 1,027 licences to Arab and foreign investors for projects that would help create 52,964 jobs. Most are industrial and service-oriented schemes.
Unemployment in Yemen is around 25 percent.

YIA grants tax breaks, exempts projects from custom tariffs and leases land at what it says are nominal fees as part of efforts to lure foreign investors into one of the Arab world's most impoverished states.
Yemen, a country of 16 million people, is a small oil producer. Its economy, hit by a brief civil war, is slowly recovering under reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund in 1995.
